subject: Fee-slice vs term-wide cap — proposed split options for MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: S. Hart (Acme Legal) <s.hart@acme.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Revisit liability cap construct for MSA/Order Form

Jasmine —

Thanks for the quick call this morning. As we discussed internally, Acme is comfortable with a limitation of liability approach but we need clarity on two items before we can proceed to countersign:

1) Whether the cap is calculated per billing period (annualized) or once for the entire contract term (aggregate).
2) If the cap is based on fees paid in the prior 12 months, what multiple applies (1x, 2x, tiered multiples).

Our commercial team prefers an annualized cap with a 1x previous-12-months floor, but legal is pushing for a term-wide 2x fees cap for a three-year commitment. Please share Redwood's preferred fallback and a short rationale so we can escalate internally.

Also, please attach your redlines to the Order Form and the MSA so we can mark up our side.

Best,
Sam Hart
Senior Counsel — Commercial Contracts
Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Revisit liability cap construct for MSA/Order Form

Sam —

Appreciate the clear summary. For transparency: Redwood's commercial default is to offer two practical options depending on buying posture — we outline both below so Acme can pick the one that best maps to commercial risk appetite. Attached is a short note and our redlined MSA highlighting the cap language.

Option A — Annualized slice (preferred for bigger, variable-consumption customers)
- Cap = greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $250k floor; applies on a rolling 12-month billing window.
- Rationale: ties exposure to recent spend; avoids oversized tails after scale-downs; helps customers with predictable monthly budgets.

Option B — Term aggregate multiple (preferred for contract simplicity / service-level commitments)
- Cap = 2x fees paid over the initial 12-month period (or 1x for customers that require a lower multiple as a concession).
- Rationale: simple to administer; aligns with common enterprise practice when there is a multi-year commitment.

Carve-outs we typically accept (and can enumerate in a short exhibit): gross negligence and willful misconduct, IP indemnity losses, amounts subject to third-party claims preserved by statute, and customer data breach remediation tied to Redwood's negligence. We will not accept unlimited consequential damages; instead we accept expressly listed consequential carve-outs (e.g., losses related to third-party fraud triggered by a failure to secure credentials if Redwood materially failed to follow required practices).

Next steps:
1) If Acme prefers Option A, we can provide an example calculation using your expected Year 1 consumption (attach spreadsheet).
2) If Acme prefers Option B but wants a 1x cap, we need commercial approval to reduce to 1x; that typically requires a committed minimum or prepayment structure.

Cc'ing Karthik for pricing implications.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu

Subject: Re: Revisit liability cap construct for MSA/Order Form — legal comments

Jasmine / Karthik —

Reviewed Sam's note and your proposed options. High-level legal guidance:

1) Prefer Option A (annualized rolling window) for mid-market customers — it limits Redwood's forward-looking exposure and maps to our billing cadence. Implementation nuance: include an express computation example in the Order Form and a data-exchange clause so Acme can verify the prior-12-month fees if disputed.

2) If customer insists on a term aggregate cap, prefer 2x of annualized fees (calculated on Year 1 forecast) for three-year deals. Reducing to 1x should be tied to either (a) a minimum annual commitment, or (b) an upfront retainer that covers a portion of estimated Year 1 consumption.

3) Carve-outs: we should keep IP indemnity and gross negligence/willful misconduct outside the cap. For cyber/data incidents, limit Redwood's exposure to third-party forensic/remediation costs but keep statutory consumer redress (if any) carved out to the extent required by law. Avoid open-ended consequential damage carve-outs — instead, accept narrowly drafted consequential categories with thresholds.

4) Add audit / reconciliation mechanics: vendor invoices + customer billing statement feed + 30-day cure window for disputes.

I'll mark up the MSA with the precise language and a short exhibit for the Order Form. Marcus — please confirm if finance is comfortable with the floor numbers Jasmine suggested ($250k) or prefers a sliding scale tied to ARR.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: see Jasmine's MSA redline (I'll add clause language in a follow-up).

Team —

Quick commercial note: the $250k floor in Option A is reasonable for this type of account, but if Acme wants a 1x term cap we should ask for one of the following as tradeoffs: 12-month committed spend, an upfront first-year prepayment equal to 25% of forecast, or a 24-month price lock. Any of those will materially reduce downside.

Karthik — happy to run sensitivity in the attached OrderForm_Acme_fee-projection_20280712.xlsx and produce two model outputs (1x term cap vs 2x term cap vs annualized 1x + $250k floor). If Acme provides forecasted consumption we can present exact numbers.

Sam —

Thanks for the quick loop on this. After internal alignment we propose the following, to keep momentum while protecting both sides:

- Primary proposal (recommended): Option A — Rolling 12-month cap = greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months, or (ii) $250,000. We will add an exhibit with a worked example and the reconciliation mechanics Laura suggested.

- Secondary fallback (if Acme prefers a term-wide number): 2x of forecasted Year 1 fees for the initial term. If Acme asks to reduce to 1x we will require one of Marcus' commercial mitigations (committed minimum, prepayment, or price lock).

- Carve-outs: Redwood to accept the standard carve-outs (IP indemnity, gross negligence/willful misconduct). For cyber/data incidents, Redwood is willing to accept remediation and third-party forensic costs outside the cap up to a reasonable upper bound; we'll list the categories explicitly in Exhibit B. Consequential damages remain disclaimed except for narrowly defined categories tied to Redwood's gross negligence.

Please confirm which path Acme prefers and, if Option B is chosen, provide Year 1 consumption forecast so Marcus can produce the modeled cap numbers. If agreeable, we can turn the MSA redline into a clean counterparty within 48 hours and route for signature.
